subject: science
passage: In his treatise the Aryabhatiya, completed in 499 CE, the Indian mathematician and astronomer Aryabhata proposed that the stars only appear to move westward across the night sky. The real motion, he argued, is the Earth turning on its axis, much as a person in a moving boat sees trees on the shore seem to move backward. Most astronomers of his era, in India and elsewhere, held that the Earth stood still, and several later Indian scholars rejected his idea. The view that the Earth rotates gained wide acceptance only many centuries afterward.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Aryabhata was the first person in history to suggest that the Earth moves.
choices.B: Most astronomers in Aryabhata's era believed that the Earth stood still.
choices.C: Later Indian scholars improved Aryabhata's idea until it was widely accepted.
choices.D: Aryabhata argued that the Earth rotates, an idea that was not widely accepted in his time.

explanation.why: The text first presents Aryabhata's proposal that the Earth turns on its axis and then qualifies it: most astronomers of his era disagreed, later scholars rejected it, and the idea was widely accepted "only many centuries afterward." The main idea combines his claim with its cool reception.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text never compares Aryabhata with anyone earlier, so it does not support "first person in history."
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is a supporting detail; it leaves out Aryabhata's own proposal, which is the text's focus.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says several later Indian scholars rejected the idea, not that they improved it.
explanation.D: Correct. This captures both parts of the text: Aryabhata's argument and the fact that it was not widely accepted for centuries.
